metadata.title: [FEATURE]: Support configurable canonical resource URL for RFC 9728 Protected Resource Metadata
metadata.author: jaygeorgenorstella

description:
<!--
💡 Tip: When suggesting a feature, provide a high-level epic and concrete user stories.
Include markdown examples, Mermaid diagrams, and MCP standards where appropriate.

Feel free to include feature requests to develop new components, MCP servers, tools, integrations, etc.
-->

### 🧭 Type of Feature

Please select the most appropriate category:

- [ ] Enhancement to existing functionality


### 🧭 Epic

Title: Allow operators to configure a stable resource identifier for RFC 9728 metadata
so MCP clients can complete the Auth0 OAuth flow without registering every UUID-based
CF server URL as a separate Auth0 API.

Goal: When a virtual server's resource identifier (the resource field in the RFC 9728
Protected Resource Metadata response) is a UUID-based URL (/servers/{uuid}/mcp), MCP
clients include that URL as the resource parameter in authorization requests to Auth0
(per RFC 8707). Auth0 rejects it with access_denied: Service not found because only
registered API identifiers are accepted. The fix must remain RFC 9728 compliant.

Why now: This blocks the standard MCP OAuth discovery flow for any deployment that uses
a shared Auth0 API identifier rather than registering every individual CF server URL.
Operators are forced to pass tokens manually, which breaks MCP clients that expect to
handle OAuth automatically (Claude.ai, MCPJam Inspector, mcp-remote).

⚠️ RFC 9728 Constraint
RFC 9728 Section 3.1 (emphasis added):
"The resource value returned MUST be identical to the protected resource's resource
identifier value into which the well-known URI path suffix was inserted to create the URL
used to retrieve the metadata."

This means: if the metadata URL is
https://gateway.example.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/servers/{uuid}/mcp,
the resource field MUST be https://gateway.example.com/servers/{uuid}/mcp.

Simply substituting oauth_config.resource for resource_base_url in
server_service.py:get_oauth_protected_resource_metadata() violates this requirement
and would cause compliant clients to reject the metadata. A correct implementation must
ensure the resource field matches the URL from which the metadata was served.

---

### 🧑🏻‍💻 User Story 1
As a: CF operator integrating with Auth0
I want: to configure a stable, human-readable canonical URL for a virtual server that
is both served as the metadata endpoint AND used as the resource identifier in the RFC
9728 response
So that: I can pre-register one stable URL in Auth0 once (not a UUID that changes when
I recreate the server), and MCP clients can complete the OAuth flow without any workaround

### ✅ Acceptance Criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: operator sets a canonical_url on a virtual server
  Given a virtual server configured with:
    oauth_enabled = true
    canonical_url = "https://gateway.nxp.example.com/mcp"
  When CF serves RFC 9728 metadata
  Then the metadata is available at:
    https://gateway.nxp.example.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp
  And the response contains:
    "resource": "https://gateway.nxp.example.com/mcp"
  And the MCP endpoint continues to work at /servers/{uuid}/mcp (unchanged)

Scenario: no canonical_url set — fallback to existing behaviour
  Given a virtual server with no canonical_url configured
  When CF serves RFC 9728 metadata
  Then the metadata URL and resource field remain the current UUID-based URL
  And behaviour is identical to CF v1.0.0 (no regression)
```

---

### 🧑🏻‍💻 User Story 2

As an: MCP client (Claude.ai, MCPJam Inspector, mcp-remote)
I want: the resource value in the protected resource metadata to be a URL that Auth0
recognises as a registered API
So that: I can include resource=<value> in the authorization request per RFC 8707
and receive a valid token without an access_denied error

### ✅ Acceptance Criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: end-to-end OAuth flow with Auth0 using a stable canonical URL
  Given the virtual server has canonical_url = "https://gateway.nxp.example.com/mcp"
  And Auth0 has "https://gateway.nxp.example.com/mcp" registered as an API
  When an MCP client follows the RFC 9728 discovery flow
  Then the client requests a token with resource=https://gateway.nxp.example.com/mcp
  And Auth0 accepts the request and issues a token
  And CF accepts the token (validating aud against canonical_url or oauth_config.resource)
```
---

### 📐 Design Sketch (optional)

Include a diagram, sketch, or flow (use [Mermaid](https://mermaid.js.org/) if desired):

Current flow (broken with UUID resource URL):

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Client
    participant CF as ContextForge
    participant Auth0

    Client->>CF: GET /servers/{uuid}/mcp (no token)
    CF-->>Client: 401 resource_metadata=".../{uuid}/mcp"

    Client->>CF: GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/servers/{uuid}/mcp
    CF-->>Client: { "resource": "http://cf/servers/{uuid}/mcp" }

    Client->>Auth0: /authorize?resource=http://cf/servers/{uuid}/mcp
    Auth0-->>Client: 400 access_denied — UUID URL not a registered API
```


Proposed flow (stable canonical URL, RFC 9728 compliant):

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Client
    participant CF as ContextForge
    participant Auth0

    Client->>CF: GET /servers/{uuid}/mcp (no token)
    CF-->>Client: 401 resource_metadata=".../.well-known/.../mcp" (canonical path)

    Client->>CF: GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp
    CF-->>Client: { "resource": "https://gateway.nxp.example.com/mcp" }

    Client->>Auth0: /authorize?resource=https://gateway.nxp.example.com/mcp
    Auth0-->>Client: 302 auth code (registered API accepted)

    Client->>CF: GET /servers/{uuid}/mcp  Authorization: Bearer <token>
    CF->>CF: validate token aud == canonical_url ✓
    CF-->>Client: 200 MCP response
```
Key implementation points:

canonical_url is an optional field on the server model. When set, CF:
Derives the well-known metadata path from canonical_url (per RFC 9728 §3.1)
Serves the metadata at that well-known path (in addition to the UUID-based path)
Returns canonical_url as the resource field in the metadata
Accepts tokens whose aud matches canonical_url (in addition to oauth_config.resource)
The UUID-based MCP endpoint (/servers/{uuid}/mcp) continues to function unchanged.
The resource_metadata URL in the WWW-Authenticate 401 response points to the
canonical well-known path when canonical_url is set.

---

### 🔗 MCP Standards Check
 
 No breaking changes to existing MCP-compliant integrations
- [ ] Change adheres to current MCP specifications
- [ ] No breaking changes to existing MCP-compliant integrations
The proposed canonical_url field is additive. Existing servers without it continue to
use the auto-generated UUID-based URL. The RFC 9728 constraint (metadata URL ↔ resource
field must match) is respected by serving the metadata AT the canonical well-known path.

---

### 🔄 Alternatives Considered

Substitute oauth_config.resource for resource_base_url in the metadata response
— violates RFC 9728 §3.1 which requires the resource field to match the URL from which
the metadata was fetched. Strict clients would reject the metadata. Rejected.

Register every CF UUID server URL in Auth0 — UUIDs are unstable (recreating a server
gives a new UUID); registering hundreds of URLs per environment is not operationally
feasible. Rejected as a general solution (acceptable for a fixed production server
as a short-term workaround).

Require clients to override the audience — only works for clients that support
explicit audience configuration (Cursor). Breaks Claude.ai and mcp-remote automatic
flows. Rejected.

---

### 📓 Additional Context

RFC references: RFC 9728 §3.1 (resource field MUST match metadata URL), RFC 8707
(resource indicators), draft-ietf-oauth-client-id-metadata-document (CIMD for clients
without pre-registration).
MCP spec: [modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-03-26/basic/authorization](http://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-03-26/basic/authorization)  —
defines how resource metadata discovery feeds into the authorization request.

I have another request to change the admin UI to expose oauth_config.resource which I have not posted it.
